```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# a)

```{r}
set.seed(123)
n1 <- 30
phi <- 0.5
x1 <- arima.sim(n = n1, list(ar = phi))
plot(x1, type = "o", main = "Simulated AR(1): phi=0.5, n=30", ylab = "Yt")
```

# b)

```{r}
# Fit model and plot residuals
fit1 <- arima(x1, order = c(1, 0, 0), include.mean = FALSE)
res1 <- residuals(fit1)
plot(res1, main = "Residuals of AR(1) Fit")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```
The residuals seems to behave like random noise, envelopped between -2 and +2.

# c)

```{r}
# Normal QQ Plot
qqnorm(res1)
qqline(res1)
```
Most of the points align roughly with the normality line suggestiong a good fit despite some deviation in the tails.

# d)

```{r}

# Sample ACF of residuals
acf(res1, main = "ACF of AR(1) Residuals")
```
The plot does not support the AR(1) specification. In a perfect model, all spikes should stay within the blue dashed lines. A significant spike at Lag 3 suggests that there is still a relationship in the data that the AR(1) didn't capture.

# e)

```{r}
# Ljung-Box Statistic (K=8)
Box.test(res1, lag = 8, type = "Ljung-Box", fitdf = 1)
```

This does not support the AR(1) specification. Since the p-value ($0.018$) is less than $0.05$, we reject the null hypothesis that the residuals are white noise.

# f)

```{r}
set.seed(456)
# (a) Simulate and Plot
n2 <- 48
phi_vec <- c(1.5, -0.75)
x2 <- arima.sim(n = n2, list(ar = phi_vec))
plot(x2, type = "o", main = "Simulated AR(2): n=48", ylab = "Yt")
```

```{r}
# (b) Fit model and plot residuals
fit2 <- arima(x2, order = c(2, 0, 0), include.mean = FALSE)
res2 <- residuals(fit2)
plot(res2, type = "o", main = "Residuals of AR(2) Fit")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```
The residuals seems to behave like random noise, envelopped between -2 and +2.

```{r}
# (c) Normal QQ Plot
qqnorm(res2)
qqline(res2)
```
Most of the points align roughly with the normality line suggestiong a good fit despite some slight deviation in the tails.

```{r}
# (d) Sample ACF of residuals
acf(res2, main = "ACF of AR(2) Residuals")
```
The good fit still hold because only the 15th spike cross the blue dashed line probably due to the small sample size.

```{r}
# (e) Ljung-Box Statistic (K=12)
Box.test(res2, lag = 12, type = "Ljung-Box", fitdf = 2)
```
## Conclusion: 

With a p-value of 0.77, we cannot reject the null hypothesis. This confirms that the residuals are independently distributed (white noise).
